title: Mermaid Syntax Fundamentals Questionnaire
concept: Reading and writing Mermaid flowchart syntax

questions.prompt: Which first line declares a flowchart whose main reading direction is left to right?
questions.explanation: Correct: `flowchart LR` selects the flowchart grammar and left-to-right direction. Incorrect options: `sequenceDiagram LR` selects the wrong diagram family and does not use flowchart direction this way; `flowchart TD` is valid but requests top-to-bottom layout.

questions.prompt: In `Gateway[API gateway]`, which part should other Mermaid edges reuse to reference the same node?
questions.explanation: Correct: `Gateway` is the stable node ID used in relationships. Incorrect options: `API gateway` is the human-facing label and may change; the square brackets select the rectangular label syntax but are not an identifier.

questions.prompt: Which definition creates a decision node that asks whether input is valid?
questions.explanation: Correct: braces create the decision diamond used for branching. Incorrect options: `[(...)]` is a database cylinder; `([...])` is a rounded terminal/process shape and does not visually communicate a decision.

questions.prompt: Which line labels the outgoing branch from `Valid` to `Save` with the word Yes?
questions.explanation: Correct: text between pipes labels the edge itself. Incorrect options: `Valid[Yes]` changes the node's visible label; `%% Yes` is a source comment and is not rendered as a branch label.

questions.prompt: What is the clearest Mermaid construct for grouping several nodes inside a named service boundary?
questions.explanation: Correct: `subgraph ... end` creates a rendered group around contained nodes. Incorrect options: `classDef` defines reusable styling rather than a boundary; `Note over` belongs to sequence diagrams and annotates participants instead of grouping flowchart nodes.

questions.prompt: Which line adds a Mermaid source comment that should not become a visible diagram element?
questions.explanation: Correct: Mermaid line comments begin with `%%`. Incorrect options: `//` is common in programming languages but not the Mermaid line-comment marker; `#` is used by formats such as Markdown or YAML but is not the general Mermaid comment syntax.

questions.prompt: Why should a flowchart author avoid using bare lowercase `end` as a node definition?

options.label: It can be parsed as the keyword that closes a subgraph.
It forces the flowchart direction to right-to-left.
It is reserved exclusively for database shapes.

questions.explanation: Correct: lowercase `end` is parser-sensitive because it terminates subgraphs; quote or capitalize display text instead. Incorrect options: direction comes from declarations such as `LR`; database shapes use bracket syntax and do not reserve the word `end`.

questions.prompt: A large flowchart stops rendering after several edits. What is the strongest first debugging move?

options.label: Reduce it to the declaration and one valid relationship, then add lines back.
Add more classDef colors until the failing line becomes visible.
Replace the source with a screenshot so the parser is bypassed.

questions.explanation: Correct: minimizing the source isolates the first failing statement and preserves a reproducible text diagram. Incorrect options: styling does not locate grammar errors; replacing source with a screenshot abandons maintainability and does not explain the failure.
